recap_title: 🤖 Exciting Junior PicToBlox Recap for Young Creators!
recap_subtitle: Welcome, creative game makers! Let's explore the magical drag-and-drop code blocks and cool game projects we built in our Junior PicToBlox course. Review the sessions below:

points.title: Visual Block Programming
points.desc: PicToBlox is a visual code-editor where we create programs by simply dragging and connecting colored blocks like LEGO pieces, making coding easy and fun!

points.title: Exploring the PicToBlox UI
points.desc: We learned about the Stage (where sprites perform), Sprites Panel (our characters list), Blocks Palette (our code drawers), and Script Area (where we snap blocks).

points.title: First Motion & Looks Blocks
points.desc: We built an 'Animal Racing' project using motion blocks like 'go to' and 'glide X Y' to slide, looks blocks like 'say' and 'think', and played sounds!

points.title: Understanding Event Blocks
points.desc: Events are yellow starting blocks (hat blocks) that detect when something happens, like clicking the green flag or when a stage backdrop switches.

points.title: Repeat Control Loops
points.desc: We used 'forever' loop blocks to repeat animation actions forever, and 'wait' blocks to pause characters so they talk in turn.

points.title: Elephant Story Animation
points.desc: We created a story where background scenery changed and sprites automatically responded using 'next costume', 'show', 'hide', and 'change x by'.

points.title: If-Condition Decisions
points.desc: We used 'if () then' control blocks. They check if a statement is true (like touching a wall) and only run the blocks inside when that condition passes.

points.title: Sensing Block Triggers
points.desc: Sensing blocks are light blue hexagons. They detect mouse clicks, keyboard keys (like arrow keys), or if a sprite is touching a colored wall.

points.title: Maze Game Project
points.desc: We drew custom mazes and programmed sprites to move using coordinate changes ('change x by' and 'change y by') and bounce back if they touched red walls.

points.title: Broadcasting Messages
points.desc: Broadcasting is like shouting a secret message. One sprite sends a 'broadcast ()' block, and other sprites listen for it to trigger their scripts.

points.title: Random Numbers
points.desc: The 'pick random (1) to (10)' operator block lets Python choose surprise numbers, making objects appear at unexpected coordinates.

points.title: Jumper Frog Game
points.desc: We combined all Level 1 concepts to code a game where a frog jumps over moving bugs that appear at random times using broadcast triggers.

points.title: What is a Variable?
points.desc: A variable is like a named scorebox in the computer memory. It stores numbers or words that we can change, check, or show during our game.

points.title: Changing Variables
points.desc: We used 'set variable to (0)' to reset parameters at startup, and 'change variable by (1)' to add points every time we scored.

points.title: Basketball Physics
points.desc: We coded a basketball game where balls fell from random X coordinates. Scoring a basket increased the score, and missing ended the game with a 'stop all' block.

points.title: Interactive Clicking
points.desc: We used the 'when this sprite clicked' event block to launch actions instantly when a player clicks on target sprites during gameplay.

points.title: Showing & Hiding Monitors
points.desc: We used 'show variable' and 'hide variable' blocks to control which game stats are visible to the players on the visual stage canvas.

points.title: Introduction to My Blocks
points.desc: We explored 'My Blocks' to design custom procedures, bundling long chains of code blocks into one single reusable block to make scripts neat.

points.title: Custom Block Functions
points.desc: Using 'My Blocks' (custom blocks) to define geometric drawing steps once, and reuse them simply by calling the custom block name.

points.title: Pen Extension Blocks
points.desc: We loaded the Pen extension to draw lines on our stage. We used 'pen down' to start drawing, 'pen up' to stop, and 'erase all' to clear.

points.title: Drawing Geometric Shapes
points.desc: We computed rotation angles (90 degrees for squares) and used loop controls to draw colorful squares, triangles, and custom hexagons.

points.title: Creating Sprite Clones
points.desc: Cloning creates exact copies of sprites while the game runs. We use 'create clone of (myself)' to spawn multiple game items without copying code.

points.title: Clone Lifecycles
points.desc: Clones start actions using 'when I start as a clone', move across the screen, and disappear safely using the 'delete this clone' block.

points.title: Understanding Gravity
points.desc: We simulated falling physics by constantly changing the bird's Y coordinate down, and pulling it back up when a player presses space.

points.title: Paint Editor Tools
points.desc: We used the built-in paint tools to draw our own custom racing cars, and designed complex road track backdrops directly inside PicToBlox.

points.title: Turning & Rotating Controls
points.desc: We programmed car steering using 'turn clockwise (degrees)' and 'turn counter-clockwise (degrees)' blocks triggered by arrow keys.

points.title: Edge Bouncing
points.desc: We used the 'if on edge, bounce' motion block to keep sprites inside the game window, making them turn away if they touch borders.

points.title: Pong-ball Gameplay
points.desc: We built a retro arcade Pong game where a ball bounces off walls and players slide paddles left and right to keep the ball active.

points.title: Logic Operators: and & or
points.desc: We combined multiple conditions using green operator blocks. 'and' requires both checks to pass; 'or' triggers if at least one check is true.

points.title: Multiball Challenges
points.desc: We cloned the game balls to increase speed and complexity, programming score adjustments depending on which wall the ball hits.

points.title: Crosshair Target Aiming
points.desc: We programmed a hunter crosshair sprite that constantly follows the player's mouse pointer using the 'go to (mouse-pointer)' motion block.

points.title: Click Sensing & Shooting
points.desc: We used 'sensing: mouse down' to check if a player clicks their mouse to shoot, and combined it with 'touching (duck)' triggers.

points.title: Duck Hunter Project Part 1
points.desc: We designed spawning logic where target ducks fly across random sky backdrops, disappearing and resetting if successfully hit.

points.title: If-Else Smart Choice Block
points.desc: The 'if () then {} else {}' control block makes two-way decisions. If the condition is true, it runs the top code; otherwise, it runs the bottom code.

points.title: Sprite Ordering Layers
points.desc: We controlled which sprites appear in front using looks layer blocks, ensuring the aiming crosshair stays stacked above flying ducks.

points.title: Duck Hunter Final Polish
points.desc: We finished our game by adding ammunition countdowns, score tracking, time limits, and sound effects for a complete arcade feel.
